pool.q: The temperatures to consider for plant growth are:
options: Minimum, maximum
Base, optimal, maximum
Maximum only

pool.q: Growing Degree Days are calculated using which formula:
options: (day max + day min) - plant base
((day max + day min) / 2) - plant base
((day min + plant base) / 2)

pool.q: Plant growth is dependant on temperature
options: True
False

pool.q: How do a microcontroller's analog pins differ from ordinary GPIO pins?
options: They have an ADC that converts voltage ranges to numbers
They can only output power, never read it
They read the voltage as text
They connect only to the I2C bus
pool.explain: Digital GPIO pins only give 1 or 0 depending on a threshold; analog pins give a numerical value.
pool.evidence: they have an ADC to convert voltage ranges to numerical values

pool.q: When measuring soil moisture, one difference between resistive and capacitive moisture sensors is:
options: As moisture levels go up the voltage goes up for resistive sensors and down for capacitive sensors
As moisture levels go up the voltage goes down for resistive sensors and up for capacitive sensors
As moisture levels go up the voltage goes up for both resistive and capacitive sensors

pool.q: The SPI protocol supports:
options: Only one controller and only one peripheral
Only one controller and multiple peripherals
Multiple controllers and multiple peripherals

pool.q: The I2C protocol supports:
options: Only one controller and only one peripheral
Only one controller and multiple peripherals
Multiple controllers and multiple peripherals

pool.q: Why can't a microcontroller power an irrigation pump directly from its pins?
options: Pumps only run on solar power
Water would short-circuit the pin
Pumps understand only analog signals
Its output is too low, so the pump needs its own supply switched by an actuator
pool.explain: A relay lets a low-power signal switch the pump's separate power supply on and off.
pool.evidence: this is too low to control larger hardware, such as a water pump used for irrigation

pool.q: A relay is what type of switch:
options: Electrical
Electromechanical
Mechanical

pool.q: A relay allows:
options: A low power device to control a higher power device
A high power device to control a low power device
Runners to run a race passing a baton between them

pool.q: Actuators should always respond instantly to sensor readings:
options: True
False

pool.q: Why does the lesson say large cloud data centres are usually environmentally friendly?
options: Because they never use electricity
Because they only run at night
Because of their size and the providers' level of investment
Because they store less data than local servers
pool.explain: Scale lets cloud providers invest in efficient cooling and cleaner energy.
pool.evidence: Because of their size and the level of investment from the cloud providers, they are usually very environmentally friendly.

pool.q: To request control of an actuator and get a response from an IoT device, app code can use a:
options: Device to cloud message
Device twin
Direct method request

pool.q: IoT Hub lets any device connect without any security:
options: False
True

pool.q: IoT Hub names must be unique:
options: True
False

pool.q: In serverless computing, when does your code run?
options: All the time, on a server you manage
Only when the event it responds to happens
Once a day at midnight
Only while you are logged in to the cloud portal
pool.explain: Nothing keeps serverless code alive between events, which is why it is cheap.
pool.evidence: Your code is only run when the event happens, there is nothing keeping your code alive at other times.

pool.q: Serverless code needs to share information between events. What must you do?
options: Save it somewhere like a database rather than in memory
Keep a server running all the time
Rewrite the code in another language
Nothing — memory is kept between events
pool.explain: Each event starts fresh, so shared state has to live outside the function.
pool.evidence: you need to save it somewhere like a database rather than storing it in memory

pool.q: How are you charged for serverless code?
options: A fixed monthly fee per server
Per line of code you deploy
Per IoT device you register
For the time it runs and the memory it uses
pool.explain: That pay-per-use model makes serverless one of the cheapest ways to run code in the cloud.
pool.evidence: Instead you pay for the time your code is running, and the amount of memory used.

pool.q: When deploying a Functions App to the cloud, you need to create and deploy:
options: A Functions App only
A Functions App and a Storage Account only
A Functions App, a Storage Account, and Application Settings

pool.q: Azure Functions can be run and debugged locally:
options: True
False

pool.q: Serverless code can only be written in JavaScript and COBOL:
options: False
True

pool.q: Symmetric key encryption compares to asymmetric key encryption in which ways:
options: Symmetric key encryption is slower than asymmetric
Symmetric key encryption is more secure than asymmetric
Symmetric key encryption is faster than asymmetric, but less secure
Symmetric key encryption is slower than asymmetric, but more secure

pool.q: X.509 certificates:
options: Should never be shared between IoT devices
Can be shared between devices
Should be kept secure and never used by any devices

pool.q: Self-signed X.509 certificates are ideal for a production environment
options: True
False

pool.q: What is remote sensing?
options: Measuring soil moisture with buried sensors
Steering farm machinery by radio
Acquiring information from a distance
Storing farm data on remote servers
pool.explain: NASA does it with instruments on satellites, spacecraft and aircraft that record reflected or emitted energy.
pool.evidence: Remote sensing is the acquiring of information from a distance.

pool.q: Which four types of resolution should you consider for any Earth observation dataset?
options: Horizontal, vertical, diagonal and depth
Radiometric, spatial, spectral and temporal
Pixel, frame, colour and sound
Daily, weekly, monthly and yearly
pool.explain: Resolution depends on the platform's orbit and the instrument's design, and shapes how the data can be used.

pool.q: How do active instruments differ from passive ones?
options: Active instruments emit energy and measure the return signal; passive ones detect natural energy
Active instruments orbit the Earth; passive ones stay on the ground
Active instruments record video; passive ones take photos
Active instruments are newer models of passive ones
pool.explain: Radar is a typical active instrument; an optical camera that records reflected sunlight is passive.
pool.evidence: Active instruments emit energy and collect data based on changes in the return signal.

pool.q: What is temporal resolution?
options: The smallest horizontal distance between data points
The number of colours a sensor can detect
The date the dataset was published
The time a platform takes to orbit and revisit the same area
pool.explain: It depends on the orbit, the instrument and the swath width.
pool.evidence: Temporal resolution is the time it takes for a space-based platform to complete an orbit and revisit the same observation area.

pool.q: How do geodetic coordinates differ from Cartesian coordinates?
options: They use a flat x–y grid with an origin at (0,0)
They only describe height above sea level
They account for the curve of the Earth, using latitude, longitude and height
They are only used for indoor maps
pool.explain: Cartesian coordinates describe points on a flat grid of perpendicular axes.
pool.evidence: Geodetic coordinates account for the curve of the Earth

pool.q: What range do NASA's data processing levels cover?
options: From level 1 drafts to level 10 final releases
From level 0 raw instrument data to level 4 model output or analysis
From level A public to level D restricted data
From level 0 free data to level 4 paid data
pool.explain: Higher levels have been processed further from the raw signal.
pool.evidence: ranging from level 0 (raw instrument data at full resolution) to level 4 (model output or analysis results)

pool.q: What is a dataset's DOI used for?
options: To identify it persistently and uniquely
To encrypt the dataset
To show which satellite collected it
To record its file size
pool.explain: A Digital Object Identifier keeps pointing to the same dataset or document over time.
pool.evidence: The Digital Object Identifier (DOI) is a persistent identifier that is used to uniquely identify objects including datasets and documents.
